name: Pura Dalem Agung Padangtegal
deity: Hyang Widhi in the form of Shiva the Transformer
significance: The main temple of the three-temple group inside Ubud's Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, standing in the south-western part of the grounds. Thought to have been raised around 1350, it remains a working centre of ritual life for the Padangtegal community.

name: Pura Rambut Siwi
deity: Dang Hyang Nirartha (his hair relic; sea temple)
significance: A cliff-top sea temple on the Jembrana coast of western Bali, counted among the island's most important pura segara. Its red-brick shrines carry reliefs of scenes from the Arjuna Wiwaha, and a cave below the site holds a water temple guarded by a statue of the priest Nirartha.
story: The name means roughly 'hair worship', from the legend that Nirartha left a lock of his hair here to protect the temple.

name: Pura Maospahit
deity: Ratu Ayu Mas Maospahit and Ida Bhatara Lingsir Sakti
style: Balinese, bare red brick in the Majapahit manner
significance: A Denpasar temple whose surviving main shrine, the Candi Raras Maospahit, is credited to the architect Sri Kbo Iwa in 1278. A second shrine for wayang performance was added in 1553 by the architect I Pasek under the Badung kingdom, and the bare red brickwork recalls thirteenth-century Majapahit building.

name: Pura Parahyangan Agung Jagatkarta
deity: The perfect divine nature, with deified ancestors including King Siliwangi of Pajajaran
significance: A large modern temple on the slopes of Mount Salak, begun in 1995 through the joint labour of the Hindu Nusantara community and serving as a Pura Kahyangan Jagad for devotees around Greater Jakarta. Its Padmasana, Balai Pasamuan Agung and paduraksa gates are finished, but the compound as a whole is not.
story: The site marks the belief that Prabu Siliwangi of Pakuan Pajajaran attained moksha here together with his soldiers.
